teacher_evidence_manifest.rule: public-context witnesses, then actual rejected-candidate harm, then parent failures; ties by source ID

by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and the asset fits an Arizona category.
by_task.procedure: Treat every statutory dollar limit as a cap, not an eligibility threshold. Include § 33-1125(1) for wearing apparel above $500, § 33-1125(2) for a musical instrument above $400, § 33-1125(8) for a motor vehicle above $15,000, and § 33-1125(10) for a firearm above $2,000. Include § 33-1101(A), not subsection (B), only when the property contains a dwelling that the debtor uses as a residence.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify jewelry as wearing apparel; § 33-1125(4) is limited to engagement and wedding rings. Non-ring jewelry does not qualify under § 33-1125(1), § 33-1125(4), or § 33-1123. Do not apply the homestead exemption to a nonresidential property interest.

by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and the asset fits an Arizona category.
by_task.procedure: Treat statutory dollar limits as caps, not eligibility thresholds, and report the lesser of asset value and the applicable cap. Include § 33-1101(A), not subsection (B), only for a dwelling used as the debtor's residence. Section 33-1123 is limited to household furniture, furnishings, household goods, consumer electronic devices, and appliances; do not use it for wearing apparel, jewelry, or musical instruments.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify jewelry as wearing apparel; § 33-1125(4) is limited to engagement and wedding rings. Non-ring jewelry does not qualify under § 33-1125(1), § 33-1125(4), or § 33-1123. Do not apply the homestead exemption to a nonresidential property interest.

operations.rationale: In source 274 EC, the parent omitted qualifying wearing apparel solely because its value exceeded § 33-1125(1)'s $500 cap, while the target retained that exemption. Source 251 similarly supports category eligibility for an above-cap musical instrument and shows the separate false-positive risk of treating nonresidential property as an Arizona homestead.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then make a mandatory final check for 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) on each debtor-owned asset. Section 522(d)(5) protects any property and remains an additional alternative even when § 522(d)(1), (2), (3), or (4) applies. Dollar ceilings limit protection rather than eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, omit § 522(d)(5) because another paragraph applies, or repeat a citation.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is allowable and an eligible asset-exemption pair needs a claim value.
by_task.procedure: Calculate every alternative independently. Use the lesser of asset value and $4,450 under § 522(d)(2), $700 per item under § 522(d)(3), or $1,875 under § 522(d)(4); for jointly owned jewelry of two debtors, § 522(m) makes the § 522(d)(4) ceiling $3,750. Then always value the separate § 522(d)(5) alternative: use the lesser of asset value and $15,425 for one debtor or $30,850 for jointly owned property of two debtors. Because alternatives are evaluated independently, the full unused § 522(d)(1) amount is available; do not reduce § 522(d)(5) merely because no residence claim is listed.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because a specific paragraph applies or the asset is not a residence, and do not use only its $1,475 base amount. Do not exceed $700 per item under § 522(d)(3) or treat that paragraph as covering firearms, jewelry, or other unlisted categories.

operations.rationale: Current EC parents in sources 265, 266, 270, and 271 omitted the independent § 522(d)(5) alternative. Current EV parents repeatedly used only $1,475 instead of the independent $15,425 or $30,850 ceiling in sources 272, 273, and 275, and source 263 also failed to apply § 522(m)'s doubled jewelry ceiling. The update distinguishes missing alternatives from wrong amounts and preserves the category limits on § 522(d)(3).

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and the debtor owns the property.
by_task.procedure: For each debtor-owned asset, make a separate final check for 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 and include it once, whether or not a federal or specific Pennsylvania exemption also applies and whether or not value exceeds its limit.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not invent a specific Pennsylvania category, use a category belonging to a different kind of property, or treat a firearm, jewelry, or other adornment as wearing apparel under § 8124(a)(1).

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and § 8123 is evaluated.
by_task.procedure: Report § 8123 independently for every debtor-owned asset. Use the asset value when it is below the applicable ceiling; otherwise use $300 for one debtor or $600 for jointly owned property of two married debtors. Keep this alternative even when a federal or specific Pennsylvania exemption also applies.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not report the ceiling when the asset value is lower, omit § 8123 because another exemption applies, or use § 8124(a)(3) unless the property is a qualifying sewing machine.

operations.rationale: In source 261 EC, the parent omitted § 8123 from two debtor-owned assets; in EV it omitted § 8123 from one asset and reported the $600 joint ceiling instead of the lower $435 asset value for another. Source 263 EV omitted Pennsylvania alternatives entirely. The revision makes the independent final check and lesser-of calculation explicit without broadening any specific category.
